text:
General Background Information
Advances in whole-genome sequencing (WGS) have enabled large-scale surveillance of bacterial pathogens. The National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) has public repositories such as Pathogen Detection system, which integrate thousands of foodborne pathogens genomes, such as Salmonella, which are generated through routine surveillance and research efforts. These resources provide a powerful framework to study plasmid prevalence and diversity across lineages, sources, and periods of time. The objective of this study is to characterize plasmid incidence in Salmonella using publicly available WGS data. This could provide insights into how frequently plasmids are detected and how their presence may vary across sources. e.g. clinical, enviroment, food, etc.

Description of data and data source
The data used in this analysis will be obtained from two publicly available NCBI resources:
NCBI Pathogen Detection (PD) The database includes assembled genomes, isolation source, collection date, and geographic information.
NCBI Datasets – Genomes The database includes assembled genomes, genome annotations, assembly statistics, and annotation files that can be used to identify plasmid-associated sequences or plasmid replicon types.
Together, these datasets contain genomic and metadata information necessary to assess the presence or absence of plasmids across a large collection of Salmonella isolates.

title: Data Analysis Project: Plasmid incidence in Salmonella per source attribution
text:
Questions/Hypotheses to be addressed
This analysis will address the following research questions:
Does plasmid incidence vary across different Salmonella serovars?
Are there observable patterns in plasmid presence associated with isolate with other factors, such as source (e.g., human, poultry, environmental) or collection year?
Based on existing literature, the hypothesis is that higher plasmid incidence is expected in isolates associated with food-animal production and clinical sources due to selective pressures such as antimicrobial use.

  separate_rows(AMR.genotypes, sep = ",") %>%
  mutate(
    AMR_gene = str_trim(AMR.genotypes),
    AMR_gene = na_if(AMR_gene, "None")
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(AMR_gene)) %>%
  #Keeping only the COMPLETED profiles
  filter(str_detect(AMR_gene, "=COMPLETE")) %>%     
  mutate(AMR_gene = str_remove(AMR_gene, "=COMPLETE"))

      # Sulfonamides

      # Trimethoprim (often co-resistance with sul)

      # Quinolones (including efflux pumps)

      # Aminoglycosides (broadened pattern)
      str_detect(AMR_gene, "aad|aph\\(|aac\\(|armA|^rmt|^ant") ~ "Aminoglycoside",
      
      # Phenicols (chloramphenicol family)

      # Glycopeptides

      # Rifamycins

amr_long <- isolates1 %>%
  # Keep isolates even if no AMR genes
  mutate(AMR.genotypes = if_else(

  )) %>%
  # Split genes into rows
  separate_rows(AMR.genotypes, sep = ",") 


# Assign antimicrobial class

amr_long <- amr_long %>%
   mutate(
      AMR_class = case_when(
      # === 1. No AMR ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "None") ~ "No AMR",
      
      # === 2. Beta-lactams ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "^bla") ~ "Beta_lactam",
      
      # === 3. Tetracyclines ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "tet") ~ "Tetracycline",
      
      # === 4. Sulfonamides ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "^sul") ~ "Sulfonamide",
      
      # === 5. Trimethoprim ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "^dfr") ~ "Trimethoprim",
      
      # === 6. Quinolones: target mutations & protection proteins ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "gyrA|gyrB|parC_|parE_|^qnr|^oqx|^qepA") ~ "Quinolone",
      
      # === 7. Aminoglycosides: modifying enzymes (broadened) ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "aad|aph\\(|aac\\(|armA|^rmt|^ant|^aphA|^aacA") ~ "Aminoglycoside",
      
      # === 8. Phenicols (chloramphenicol family) ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "floR|^cat|^cml|^gar") ~ "Phenicol",  
      
      # === 9. Macrolides: including esterases (estT/estX) ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "erm|^mef|^mph|^msr|^ere|^est") ~ "Macrolide",  

      # === 10. Lincosamides ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "^lnu") ~ "Lincosamide",
      
      # === 11. Fosfomycin ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "^fos") ~ "Fosfomycin",
      
      # === 12. Colistin/Polymyxin: mcr enzymes + pmr regulators ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "^mcr|^pmrA_|^pmrB_") ~ "Colistin",  
      
      # === 13. Glycopeptides ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "^van") ~ "Glycopeptide",
      
      # === 14. Rifamycins ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "^arr") ~ "Rifamycin",
      
      # === 15. Bleomycin resistance ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "^ble") ~ "Bleomycin",  
      
      # === 16. Streptothricin resistance ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "^sat") ~ "Streptothricin",  

      # === 17. Streptogramin/Virginiamycin resistance ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "^vat") ~ "Streptogramin", 
      
      # === 18. Multidrug Efflux Pumps (RND family + tmex/toprJ) ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "^mds|^acr|^mex|^ade|^cme|^amrB|^tmex|^toprJ") ~ "Efflux Pump",
      
      # === 19. MDR Transcriptional Regulators (upregulate efflux) ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "^ramR_|^soxR_|^marR|^rob") ~ "MDR Regulator",

      # === 20. Gentamicin ===
      str_detect(AMR.genotypes, "grd") ~ "Gentamicin",
           
      # === 21. Default ===
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  )

  set_engine("lm") %>%

  set_engine("lm") %>% 
  fit(Protein.coding ~ Length, data = genomes1)
